partners.mechanism_chain: MAP3K7 (HGNC:6872) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-71277); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-71277) —LEADS_TO→ Spondylocarpal dysplasia (HP:0004472); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-71277) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); IKBKG (HGNC:17904) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-71277); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-71277) —LEADS_TO→ Skin defects (HP:0000951); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-71277) —LEADS_TO→ Cataract (HP:0000511). Both cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome (CSFS) and incontinentia pigmenti (IP) involve the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. CSFS arises from haploinsufficiency of MAP3K7, leading to disruption of this pathway and downstream phenotypes. IP arises from loss-of-function mutations in IKBKG, which also disrupts the NF-kappaB pathway, albeit through a different mechanism (affecting the upstream IKK complex), leading to its characteristic phenotypes. The shared convergence on the NF-kappaB pathway, despite different direct genetic causes and specific functional consequences within the pathway, forms the mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in MAP3K7 that exhibit gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in relevant cellular models for either disease would falsify the proposed haploinsufficiency mechanism. _(variant: rs145877679)_
